mechanism_narrative: The observed slight upward trend in RETAIL_REC mobility over the last two weeks, moving from -34.6% to -32.0%, indicates a gradual and sustained return to retail and recreation activities, which will continue over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean of the last 28 days, despite the recent upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: A continued increase in WORKPLACES mobility, building on the slight recovery from -36.3% to -35.6% in the last two weeks, signifies more people returning to their physical workplaces, which will directly translate into increased footfall for retail and recreation establishments during weekdays.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by at least 0.5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises by at least 0.5 points week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days does not increase compared to the previous 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: The current high RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates a preference for staying home. If RESIDENTIAL mobility begins to decline while RETAIL_REC shows any positive momentum, it signals a significant shift in behavior from home-based activities to out-of-home retail and recreation.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls by at least 0.5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL falls by at least 0.5 points week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase compared to the previous 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained low and stable TRANSIT mobility, hovering around -30%, indicates that public transport use remains significantly suppressed, likely due to ongoing restrictions or public health concerns. This will continue to limit access to and footfall in urban retail and recreation centers.
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility increases by more than 5 points over the next 28 days, leading to an increase in RETAIL_REC.

mechanism_narrative: The recent sharp decline in GROCERY_PHARM mobility from -10.4% to -12.9% at t-0w, if sustained or deepened, suggests a broader reduction in essential out-of-home trips, indicating increased caution or tightening of local conditions, which will negatively impact non-essential RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls by more than 1 point week-on-week
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM recovers by more than 1 point week-on-week, and RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next 7 days.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility and an increase in WORKPLACES mobility indicates a significant shift from staying at home to engaging in out-of-home work activities. This combined movement will drive a substantial increase in RETAIL_REC as people spend less time at home and more time in commercial areas.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls by at least 1 point AND WORKPLACES rises by at least 1 point week-on-week
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL falls and WORKPLACES rises as specified, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase compared to the previous 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The consistently high and slightly increasing RESIDENTIAL mobility (from 8.1% to 9.4%) over the last four weeks indicates a persistent preference or necessity for staying at home, which directly limits opportunities and willingness for out-of-home retail and recreation activities.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility declines by more than 2 points over the next 28 days, and RETAIL_REC increases.

mechanism_narrative: As the decision point is mid-November, the fluctuating but generally lower PARKS mobility compared to earlier periods (e.g., t-3w vs t-0w) suggests a seasonal decline in outdoor activities due to colder weather. This reduction in general outdoor movement will indirectly suppress overall out-of-home mobility, including RETAIL_REC.
failure_condition: PARKS mobility increases significantly over the next 14 days, or RETAIL_REC increases despite declining PARKS mobility.
